name: Dr. Dre
hook: N.W.A's main producer left the group in 1991 and built G-funk, an entire West Coast sound, largely out of George Clinton's catalogue.
blurb: Andre Young, known as Dr. Dre, was N.W.A's main producer. He left the group in 1991 and co-founded Death Row Records with Suge Knight. His 1992 solo album 'The Chronic' started G-funk, a slower style built on synthesizers and funk samples, and made it the main West Coast sound of the early-to-mid 1990s. It was built heavily on George Clinton and Parliament-Funkadelic's music, mostly uncredited when it came out: 'Fuck Wit Dre Day' alone uses several of their recordings, including the chant from Clinton's own solo hit 'Atomic Dog'. Dre later founded Aftermath Entertainment in 1996, signed Eminem in 1998, and in 2006 co-founded Beats Electronics, sold to Apple in 2014, though those years sit outside this map. Also part of the record: in 1991 Dre pleaded no contest to assaulting the television host Dee Barnes and was sentenced to probation, and a related civil suit was settled. He has since admitted the assault, which is first recorded on this map at N.W.A's own entry.
